sentences.text: Acresuchus, meaning "Acre crocodile," is an extinct genus of medium-sized caiman found in western Brazil and Venezuela.
The genus contains only one known species, Acresuchus pachytemporalis.
The holotype specimen UFAC-2507 is a nearly complete skull found in the Solimões Formation in Acre.
A skull fragment specimen was also found in the Urumaco Formation in Venezuela.
This animal possesses large supratemporal fenestrae, which may be adaptations for large body size.
Its large supratemporal fenestrae may have aided in quicker prey capture and thermoregulation.
Blunt teeth at the back of the skull suggest it may have eaten hard-shelled animals.
The genus Acresuchus was described by Souza-Filho and colleagues in 2018.
Acresuchus likely had a diet similar to the living black caiman due to shared features and size.
Juvenile Acresuchus likely preyed on small invertebrates, while adults ate fish and small to medium-sized mammals.
Acresuchus belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
It is classified as a member of the subfamily Caimaninae, closely related to Purussaurus.
The parent group of Acresuchus is the genus Jacarea.
Acresuchus lived during the Late Miocene epoch.
It lived from the Tortonian to the Messinian stages, between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago.
